 Sri E. Rajeeva Gowda, L.L.M.
 Xlv Addl. City Civil & Sessions Judge, Bengaluru.

.... ACCUSED  (By Sri VM, Advocate for accused)
 2 S.C.No.1484/2018  * * * * *
 J U D G M E N T

The Police Sub-Inspector, Yeshwanthpura PS submitted charge sheet against the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504, 506, 307 of IPC.
2.

The brief story of the prosecution are as under:
The accused is the son of C.W.4 Smt.Lakshmi Devi and husband of the complainant by name Divya.
The accused subjected C.W.1 to physical and mental harassment.

Yashwanthapura Ps vs Mahadeva on 31 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150662812/
1
Due to such physical and mental harassment, the complainant and C.W.4 left the house and started to reside at No.10, situated at 2nd cross, Subedarpalya.
Even after that, the accused going to said house and continued to harass C.W.1 mentally and physically abusing in filthy language by demanding money.

On 17.05.2018 at 12.30 noon when the complainant and C.W.4 were in the house, the accused went there and abused in filthy language by demanding money and also with intention to kill the C.W.4, squeezed her neck and threatened with dire consequences.
Thereby the accused has committed the offences as alleged in the charge sheet.

3. The concerned police have submitted charge sheet before the concerned Judicial Magistrate,
Bangalore.
The learned Magistrate, after taking cognizance of the offences against the accused,
committed the case to the Sessions Court by complying Section 207 of CrPC by furnishing copy of the charge sheet to the accused.

After committal, the said case was numbered as SC No. 1484/2018.
4.

The charge was framed against the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504,
506, 307 of IPC.
The accused has pleaded not guilty and claims to be tried.
5. The prosecution has examined eight witnesses as PWs.1 to 8 and got marked documents at EX.P1 to P9.
The learned PP has failed to examine CWs.2 and 3 inspite of issuance of summons and warrant.
As such the prayer of the learned PP was rejected and the said witnesses CWs.2 and 3 were dropped by rejecting the prayer of the prosecution.
However liberty has been given to the prosecution for examination of the said witnesses, if the said witnesses brought before the court by the concerned police.
Moreover in the present case, the prime witnesses of the prosecution were turned hostile.
6. After completion of prosecution side evidence, this court has recorded the statements of accused as provided under Section 313 of CrPC.
The accused has denied incriminating evidence present against him and not opted to lead defence evidence nor submitted anything to the court.
The accused has complied Section 437A of CrPC.

7. Heard the arguments on both sides and perused the materials on record.
8.

The following points that arises for consideration of this court:
1. Whether the prosecution proves that the accused being the husband of CW.1 Smt.
Divya subjected her to physical and mental cruelty, unable to tolerate the physical and mental cruelty of accused, CW.1 and CW.4 Smt. Laksmidevi, being his mother left the house and started to reside separately at house No.10, situated at 2nd Cross,
Subedarpalya, even by visiting the said house accused continued to harass CW.1 physically and mentally, by abusing CW.1 in filthy language in demanding money and thereby accused has committed the offence punishable U/s.498A of Indian Penal Code, 1860?
Yashwanthapura Ps vs Mahadeva on 31 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150662812/
2 2.

Whether the prosecution proves that the accused being the husband of CW.1 Smt.
Divya and son of CW.4 Lakshmidevi, continued to harass CW.1 physically and mentally, by abusing CW.1 and CW.4 in filthy language in demanding money and thereby accused has committed the offence punishable U/s.504 of Indian Penal Code,
1860?

3. Whether the prosecution proves that the accused being the husband of CW.1 Smt.
Divya and son of CW.4 Lakshmidevi, continued to harass CW.1 physically and mentally, by abusing CW.1 and CW.4 in filthy language in demanding money, when they refused for the same, accused assaulting them with hands and on 17.05.2018 quarreling with CW.1 in demanding money, when CW.4 tried to rescue CW.1, at that time accused by squeezed her neck and attempted to kill her, when CW.1 resisted for the same, threatened to kill her and thereby accused has committed the offence punishable U/s.307 of Indian Penal Code, 1860?
4. Whether the prosecution proves that the accused being the husband of CW.1 Smt.
Divya and son of CW.4 Lakshmidevi, continued to harass CW.1 physically and mentally in demanding money, when CW.4 tried to rescue CW.1, accused threatened to kill her by causing injuries on 19.05.2018 at 12.30 p.m. came near the house of CW.1 and thereby accused has committed the offence punishable U/s.506 of Indian Penal Code, 1860?
5.
What order?

9. This Court has answered the above above points are as under:
 Point No.1: In the Negative  Point No.2: In the Negative  Point No.3: In the Negative  Point No.4: In the Negative  Point No.5: As per final order  for the following:
 R E A S O N S 10.
Points No.1 to 4: All these points are taken up together for discussions as they are related with each other and to avoid repetition.

Yashwanthapura Ps vs Mahadeva on 31 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150662812/
3
The wife of the accused by name Divya and mother of the accused by name Lakshmi Devi are vital witnesses of the prosecution.

The complaint marked at Ex.P.1 reveals how the accused has harassed CWs.1 and 4 physically and mentally and also attempted to kill C.W.4 for the sake of money from complainant abusing in filthy language and giving threat, but the wife and mother i.e. PWs.1 and 2 not supported prosecution story by not giving any evidence against the accused.
The evidence of complainant reveals that their marriage was performed in Gayathri temple at Yeshwanthpur.
She was working as Beautician and accused was an auto driver.
The accused used to consume liquor and quarreled with C.W.1, hence she went to police station and lodged complaint requesting the police to advise, except that nothing has happened.

Even it is the say of the P.W.2 Lakshmi Devi that accused during intoxicated condition used to quarrel with the complainant and due to which the complainant went to police station and lodged complaint requesting the police to advise the accused.
Except that, the both witnesses never spoken anything regarding physical and mental harassment committed by the accused towards the complainant and also anything about his attempt to kill her.

Though the complainant being the signatory to the complaint and Mahazar marked at Exs.P.1 and 2 respectively, but it is the say of the complainant that she does not know what is written in the complaint and the police never conducted Mahazar in her presence.
She has produced the marriage invitation and photos at the request of the police.

Since the evidence of PWs.1 and 2 not in accordance with the complaint and statement and also Mahazar, hence, learned PP treated the said witnesses PWs.1 and 2 as hostile and putforth the questions according to the complaint and statement of PWs.1 and 2 respectively.
Inspite of that, the learned PP failed to get any worthful evidence to believe the contents of complaint, Mahazar and statement.
As such the evidence given by PWs.1 and 2 are not acceptable as trustworthy.
11. It is necessary to note that the relative of accused by name Naveen Kumar, Manoj Kumar and Manasa have been examined by the prosecution as PWs.3, 4 and 7 respectively.
The version of PWs.3, 4 and 7 very much similar as deposed by wife and mother of accused.
The evidence given by said witnesses PWs.3, 4 and 7 contrary to their respective statements.
Hence, learned PP treated the both witnesses as hostile and cross examined with the permission of the court.
Inspite of that, the prosecution not able to get any useful evidence in support of the prosecution story.
However, the evidence of PWs.1, 2, 4 and 7 shows that the accused is the divorced husband of complainant.
Perhaps none of the independent witnesses including victims PWs.1 and 2 not given evidence in favour of the prosecution.

12. It is obvious to note that the witness P.W.6 Dr.Uma being the Medical Officer has clearly deposed that on 17.05.2018 at 2.45 p.m the witness P.W.2 Lakshmi Devi came to hospital with history of assault by her son.
The swelling was present on her left cheek.

After providing treatment,
she referred the said witness C.W.4 before E N T and accordingly she issued wound certificate as per Ex.P.8.
The said evidence has completely denied by accused counsel.
13. The police witnesses by name Rajanna and Devika Devi examined as PWs.5 and 8 respectively.
The witness Rajanna has categorically deposed that on 19.05.2018 he was the SHO of the police station, the complainant came to police station at 12.30 noon and lodged written complaint.

On the basis of the same, he has registered Cr.No.161/2018 against the accused and thereafter visited the spot and conducted Mahazar at spot in the presence of panchas as shown by the complainant as per Yashwanthapura Ps vs Mahadeva on 31 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150662812/
4 Ex.P.2.
Thereafter the complainant brought the accused to the police station.
Immediately he has carried out arrest procedure and after medical examination produced him before the court alongwith remand application and police escort.

On the same day, he has recorded statements of CWs.4 to 6 and thereafter handed over further investigation to C.W.10/P.W.8.
14.
P.W.8 i.e.
Devika Devi has collected wound certificate of P.W.2 as per Ex.P.8 on 09.08.2018 and as the investigation was completed submitted charge sheet against the accused.
The evidence given by both the police witnesses PWs.5 and 8 has completely denied by the counsel representing the accused.
It is very clear from the above discussion that neither wife nor the mother of the accused and also relatives of the accused never supported the prosecution story.
The evidence given by the said witness completely contrary to the evidence of Medical Officer and police witnesses.
So, lot of doubts arose about the occurrence of the incident as alleged against the accused.
So, it is very clear that the prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt.
As such, this court has answered the point Nos.1 to 4 in the Negative.

15. Point No.5: In view of answer of this court on points No.1 to 4, this court proceed to pass the following:
O R D E R U/s.235(1) of Cr.P.C. the accused is hereby acquitted of the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504, 506, 307 of IPC.
The bail bond and surety bond of accused stands cancelled.
